---
title: "Geometry and SGB Route A/B"
---

The in-tree `scgsim.sgb` package is SCGSim's current geometry and topology
authority. It consumes structured PDK and component semantics and must not
reconstruct geometry meaning from solver-generated labels.

`build_component_stack()` composes two explicit authorities. PDK
`LayerStack` records supply materials, process layers, Z/thickness,
conductor/solution roles, and exact host volumes. Component annotations supply
nets, ports, functional conductor regions, and topology selectors. Notebook
authors supply neither record set manually.

The public composition entry is
`build_component_stack(component=..., layer_stack=..., material_records=...,
coupon_padding_um=...)`. Padding is finite and nonnegative, in micrometres;
zero preserves the exact authored coupon. The component must carry structured
`info["component_semantics"]` with schema version 1, and the LayerStack must
declare the included solution regions and material/host facts. Missing or
ambiguous records fail rather than triggering name/bounding-box inference.

The adapter entries `build_gdsfactory_geometry_input(...)` and
`build_gds_stack_geometry_input(...)` consume the canonical component or GDS
plus its semantic stack. `SemanticGeometryBuilder` owns the lowering and
topology validation. Use the staged Palace API when a Palace mesh/config/
handoff is wanted; do not reconstruct the compiler's semantic layer records
in a notebook. Explicit component geometry may contain several disconnected
residual conductors with shared net/equipotential identity; no selector should
discard legitimate source-authored Ground regions.

## Current Surface-EPR direction

| Route | Public intent | Current state |
|---|---|---|
| Route A | Zero-thickness face-metal PEC sheets with finite bump shells | Implemented, converging |
| Route B | The closed exterior boundary shell of a finite construction metal volume is PEC; its interior is excluded from Palace solution domains and receives no tetrahedra | Implemented, converging |

Only Route A and Route B are in the current direction.

## Identity requirements

A handoff preserves:

- source SGB revision;
- semantic surface and volume identities;
- route choice and topology receipt;
- generated mesh/config identity;
- the mapping from solver entities back to semantic geometry.

External SGB revisions remain derivation history only. The in-tree
`scgsim.sgb` package is the current authority; no direct external consumer or
fallback path is implied.
